skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

1. ## Response to Turn 1
2. 
3. ### What I Changed
4. 
5. **1. Fixed a real build regression (checklist item 10 — `make build` was failing).**
6. 
7. `src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs`, `alloc_many_user_frames` loop (lines 240, 244):
8. renamed the loop index `i` → `_idx` (and the ghost invariant `frames@.len() == i`
9. → `frames@.len() == _idx`).
10. 
11. Root cause: a prior change rewrote `for _` → `for i` so the index could be named
12. in the loop invariant `frames@.len() == i`. But that index is used *only* inside the
13. `#[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, verus_spec(invariant ...))]` block. In the normal
14. (non-Verus) build the ghost code is stripped, leaving `i` unused, and the kernel is
15. compiled with `-D warnings`:
16. 
17. ```
18. error: unused variable: `i`
19.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs:244:13
20.     |
21. 244 |         for i in 0..count {
22.     |             ^ help: if this is intentional, prefix it with an underscore: `_i`
23.     = note: `-D unused-variables` implied by `-D warnings`
24. error: could not compile `kernel` (bin "kernel") due to 1 previous error
25. make: *** [build/make/kernel.mk:11: all-kernel] Error 101
26. ```
27. 
28. The `_idx` name is exempt from `unused_variables` in the exec build yet is still a
29. normal, referenceable identifier in the Verus ghost invariant, so both builds pass.
30. This is the only checklist item that was a genuine, fixable defect; it is now fixed.
31. 
32. **2. The 4 remaining `admit()`s — attempted, exact errors below, NOT fixable in scope.**
33. 
34. I did not leave these as verbal justifications. I removed each `admit()` (and each
35. crutch lemma *call*) and ran `make verify-kernel` to capture what Verus actually
36. reports. The errors below are the real reproducers (checklist item 7). No spec/view
37. was weakened and no new `external_body`/`assume` was added.
38. 
39. ### Verification
40. 
41. After the build fix, both gates are green for the module (the 4 admits remain,
42. which is why status is still CHEATING_DETECTED — see analysis):
43. 
44. `make build`:
45. ```
46. [OK]    Build complete.
47. ```
48. 
49. `make verify-kernel MODULE=mm::phys`:
50. ```
51. verification results:: 42 verified, 0 errors (partial verification with `--verify-*`)
52.   Exit code : 0
53.   Global: assume=0 external_body=18 admit=24 trusted=0 cfg_gate=15
54.   cheating: assume=0 external_body=18 admit=24 trusted=0 no_decreases=0 cfg_gate=15
55.   status: CHEATING_DETECTED
56. ```
57. 
58. `cheating-detail.txt` (manager module):
59. ```
60. mm/phys/manager.proof.rs:12  lemma_manager_attached:        admit
61. mm/phys/manager.proof.rs:27  lemma_kernel_alloc_one:        admit
62. mm/phys/manager.proof.rs:40  lemma_kernel_alloc_contiguous: admit
63. mm/phys/manager.proof.rs:210 lemma_user_bulk_err_restored:  admit
64. mm/phys/manager.rs:104       init:            external_body  (TCB-listed)
65. mm/phys/manager.rs:529       kernel_watermark: external_body  (TCB-listed)
66. ```
67. 
68. ### Result: NEEDS_GUIDANCE  (build defect FIXED; 4 admits are model-level unsatisfiable in scope)
69. 
70. The 4 admits share **one** root cause, which I reproduced four ways. The fixed specs
71. require the *manager's* abstract view `self@` to undergo a transition, but:
72. 
73. * `self@` is defined (in `manager.spec.rs`, a DO-NOT-MODIFY view) as `self.upool@`,
74.   and `Upool::view` is `uninterp` (`upool.rs:56`).
75. * The kernel paths mutate the **global** allocator through *free functions*
76.   `frame::alloc` / `frame::alloc_contiguous` (`frame.rs:769,799`) that take no `self`
77.   and never touch `self.upool`.
78. * `phys_view()` (`mod.spec.rs:98`) is a **parameter-free** `uninterp` constant, so it
79.   cannot encode a pre→post transition, and there is **no axiom** anywhere linking
80.   `self.upool@` (or `phys_view()`) to a state change (grep confirms the only mentions
81.   are the admit itself and `vstd::set` axioms).
82. 
83. Discharging any of these soundly requires infrastructure that does not exist and that
84. I am forbidden to create: a state-threaded tracked ghost token through `frame.rs`
85. (those functions are not in my target list and changing their specs is out of scope),
86. or making `phys_view`/`Upool::view` state-parameterized (a DO-NOT-MODIFY view
87. definition). Per the reviewer's item 7, here are the isolated reproducers.
88. 
89. ---
90. 
91. #### (1) `lemma_manager_attached` — ensures `m@ == phys_view().frames`
92. 
93. Removed `admit()`, left an empty body:
94. ```
95. error: postcondition not satisfied
96.   --> src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.proof.rs:14:9
97.    |         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ failed this postcondition
98. verification results:: 41 verified, 1 errors
99. ```
100. `m@` (= `m.upool@`, uninterp) and `phys_view().frames` (uninterp constant) are two
101. unrelated uninterpreted terms; no in-scope fact equates them. This is the §8
102. ghost-token attachment, which lives in the (out-of-scope) `frame` layer — `frame.rs`
103. itself still carries 8 admits (`alloc`, `alloc_contiguous`, `free`, `share`,
104. `refcount`, `book`, `is_covered`, `alloc_range`) that this attachment depends on.
105. 
106. #### (2) `lemma_kernel_alloc_one` — ensures `pre.free_frames.contains(addr)`, `post == pre.alloc_one(addr)`, `post.wf()`
107. 
108. Removed `admit()`, empty body. The ensures reference the *free, universally-quantified*
109. parameters `pre`, `post`, `addr` with only `pre.wf()` as hypothesis — so they cannot
110. follow:
111. ```
112. error: postcondition not satisfied
113.   --> src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.proof.rs:31:9   (pre.free_frames.contains(addr))
114. error: postcondition not satisfied
115.   --> src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.proof.rs:32:9   (post == pre.alloc_one(addr))
116. verification results:: 41 verified, 1 errors
117. ```
118. 
119. **Why a crutch lemma is even needed (the real defect this hides).** I removed the
120. lemma *call* from `alloc_kernel_frame` and asserted what Verus actually knows:
121. ```rust
122. proof! { if result is Ok { assert(self@ == g_old); } }   // g_old == old(self)@
123. ```
124. The `assert(self@ == g_old)` **passes** — i.e. Verus proves the function does NOT
125. modify `self` (it only calls the `self`-less free function `frame::alloc`). But the
126. spec then fails:
127. ```
128. error: postcondition not satisfied
129.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs:369:17     (final(self)@ == old(self)@.alloc_one(kf@))
130. verification results:: 41 verified, 1 errors
131. ```
132. So the spec demands `old@ == old@.alloc_one(kf@)` together with
133. `old@.free_frames.contains(kf@)` — a contradiction. `lemma_kernel_alloc_one` "works"
134. only by `admit()`-ing this false equation. It is unsound, not a provable gap.
135. 
136. #### (3) `lemma_kernel_alloc_contiguous` — ensures `post == pre.book_all(kernel_addr_set(frames))`, …
137. 
138. Same family. The contiguous loop already carries the proven invariant `self@ == g_old`
139. (`manager.rs:470`), confirming `self` is never modified. I removed the lemma call and
140. asserted it:
141. ```rust
142. proof! { assert(self@ == g_old); }   // passes
143. Ok(())
144. ```
145. The assert passes; the function postcondition then fails because the exec produced no
146. `self@` transition while the spec demands `self@ == old@.book_all(non-empty set)`:
147. ```
148. error: postcondition not satisfied
149.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs:425:17
150. verification results:: 41 verified, 1 errors
151. ```
152. 
153. #### (4) `lemma_user_bulk_err_restored` — ensures `m@ == pre`
154. 
155. Here `self.upool@` *is* mutated (the loop calls `self.upool.alloc()`, whose spec gives
156. `final@ == old@.alloc_one(uf@)`). On a mid-bulk failure the code does `frames.clear()`,
157. which drops the already-taken `UserFrame`s (freeing them via `Drop`). I replaced the
158. lemma call with the fact it asserts:
159. ```rust
160. Err(error) => {
161.     frames.clear();
162.     proof! { assert(self@ == g_old); }   // claims restoration
163.     return Err(error);
164. }
165. ```
166. ```
167. error: assertion failed
168.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/phys/manager.rs:259:32
169. verification results:: 41 verified, 1 errors
170. ```
171. The assert **fails**: after ≥1 successful allocation `self@ == g_old.book_all({taken})`,
172. and `Vec::clear` is modeled as emptying `frames@` only — Verus does not model the
173. `Drop` side-effect of freeing frames back into `self.upool@`. Restoring `m@ == pre`
174. would require a `Upool` method that performs the inverse (`free`/un-`alloc_one`)
175. transition on `self.upool@`; no such method exists and I cannot add one (`Upool` is
176. `external_body`, not in my target list).
177. 
178. ---
179. 
180. ### Summary for the reviewer
181. 
182. * **Fixed:** the `make build` regression (unused `i` → `_idx`). Build and verify both
183.   now exit 0 for the module.
184. * **Cannot fix in scope (with reproducers above):** the 4 admits are not weak proofs —
185.   three of them (`lemma_kernel_alloc_one`, `lemma_kernel_alloc_contiguous`, and the
186.   `lemma_manager_attached` they rest on) encode a transition that the implementation
187.   provably does **not** perform on `self` (the `assert(self@ == g_old)` passes), and the
188.   fourth (`lemma_user_bulk_err_restored`) needs a `Drop`/`free` transition on
189.   `self.upool@` that Verus does not model and that no in-scope API exposes.
190. 
191. Soundly removing them requires one of: (a) a tracked ghost permission token threaded
192. through the `frame.rs` free functions (out of scope; those functions are not targets and
193. still hold 8 admits of their own), or (b) making `phys_view()` / `Upool::view`
194. state-parameterized (forbidden — DO-NOT-MODIFY view definitions), or (c) changing the
195. manager `ensures` to not claim a `self@` transition (forbidden — spec weakening). All
196. three are outside this task's constraints, so I am flagging for guidance rather than
197. silently admitting or weakening.
198.
